findings.note: Warn diagnostics already collected by _evaluate_capabilities are dropped, not forwarded, on every abort path. This satisfies AC-056's "never warn-only for this id" invariant but sits against REQ-004's own sentence that diagnostics[] records "every diagnostic-worthy condition this invocation encountered, not only the first/fatal one". REQ-004's own "or jointly caused" wording would have permitted the lossless alternative (keep the per-node warn entries and add the same-id block summary alongside the abort's own entry). Impact is bounded because the underlying outcome: "warn" nodes survive inside capability_evaluations[] for every capability whose evaluation set completed -- but not for the capability that aborted mid-set, since entries are appended only after a capability is fully built.

This loose stand-in still declares definitions.projectedComponent.additionalProperties: true, which the round-2 remediation itself identified as diverging from the real, landed contracts/context-projection.schema.json (additionalProperties: false with an enumerated property set). That remediation switched install_t003_dependencies to seed the real files from ROOT/contracts/, so this file is now dead fixture content still carried as a declared output. Cleanup, not a live defect.

sys.path.insert(0, str(script_dir)) is never restored (no try/finally), leaving the plugin scripts directory permanently ahead of the stdlib on sys.path for the remainder of the process. Self-disclosed in T-004.md's Unresolved Items as a follow-on; low practical risk because every stdlib import in this module resolves before the insert.
